old: Reaching the planning limit without a detection does not itself trigger escalation.
new: Reaching the planning limit without a detection does not itself trigger escalation. At main `72d2349`, loop control treats an `ANSWER` settled after the nudge like a `REFUSE` settled after the nudge, and a first `ANSWER` outside an episode ends the turn with the answer.

`MULTI_TURN_PLANNER_PROMPT_VERSION:2026-11-26-p512-answer` (`agent/prompts.py:10–15`, `:40–50`). At `72d2349`, `ANSWER:` is a whole-reply form in the multi-turn grammar, with at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes of answer text, no directive line, and the #583 character rule with line breaks and tabs permitted (`agent/prompts.py:14`, `:119–122`; `agent/planning_loop.py:104`, `:961–988`). An Agent-mode answer settles as a completed run with `PLANNING_ANSWERED`. Its terminal message is the answer as final text, with no plan update, and ACP returns `end_turn` with `_meta` `{"runStopReason": "PLANNING_ANSWERED", "outcome": "completed"}`, unless a cancel was accepted first. When continuity is configured, the committed turn's checkpoint records `responded` and no completed task (`agent/runner.py:171–176`; `acp/spec.py:3052–3058`, `:3972–3974`, `:4024–4039`, `:4054–4057`, `:4144–4146`, `:4286–4298`, `:4310–4316`; `context/memory_continuity.py:150–158`). Known limit: the answer parser and the EDIT parser split a code fence differently when its lines are separated only by bare carriage returns, so such a reply can settle as an answer without its EDIT (PR #657).

`:240–290`). At `72d2349`, a waiting answer follows the same escalation and check-in rules as a waiting refusal (`src/optimus/agent/planning_loop.py:119–120`, `:1584–1609`, `:1627–1632`, `:1640–1647`).
